name: Offices
pitch: Brand walls and focus-friendly art for workplaces.
headline: Art for the walls your team sees every day
intro: An office wall is looked at more often than any brochure the company will ever print — usually by the same people, for years. That changes what belongs on it. Work that shouts is exhausting by month three; work that rewards a second look is still earning its place in year three.

considerations.title: Downlights and glare
considerations.text: Most offices are lit from directly above, which turns a glossy surface into a mirror. A matte acrylic face and brushed aluminium stay readable; a gloss face directly under a spotlight does not.

considerations.title: Reception sets the tone
considerations.text: The reception wall is the one visitors photograph and remember. It usually justifies the largest piece in the building.

considerations.title: Focus areas want quiet
considerations.text: Colour-field and minimal work suits desks and quiet rooms. Save the statement pieces for circulation space.

name: Cafés
pitch: Instagrammable feature walls that anchor your interior.
headline: The wall people photograph before their coffee
intro: A café's feature wall does marketing work that no ad budget matches — every photograph taken in front of it carries the room to someone who has not visited yet. It has to look good in a phone camera, in evening light, with people in front of it.

considerations.title: It will be photographed
considerations.text: Strong composition and clear colour read well in a phone camera. Fine detail disappears at the distance people shoot from.

considerations.title: Seating changes the height
considerations.text: Art above banquette seating hangs higher than gallery convention suggests, so it clears heads and stays visible across the room.

considerations.title: It has to be cleanable
considerations.text: Near a counter or a service run, brushed aluminium and PVC foam survive what MDF will not — PVC is unaffected by humidity, and MDF belongs away from wet areas.

name: Restaurants
headline: Art that sets the room before the first course
intro: A dining room is judged in the first ten seconds, mostly on atmosphere. Art carries a disproportionate share of that — it tells guests what kind of evening this is going to be, long before the menu does.

considerations.title: Low light changes everything
considerations.text: Pieces chosen under showroom lighting can vanish at dinner service. We proof against the actual light levels of the room.

considerations.title: Long walls want long work
considerations.text: Banquette runs and corridors read better with panoramic pieces than with a row of small ones.

considerations.title: Kitchens and grease travel
considerations.text: Anywhere within reach of a pass, sealed surfaces are the only sensible answer.

name: Hotels
pitch: Lobby statements and serene art for guest floors.
headline: A lobby that means somewhere, and floors that let guests rest
intro: Hotels ask two different things of art in the same building. The lobby has to say where you are and why this hotel rather than another. Guest floors have to do the opposite — recede, repeat without monotony, and never be the reason someone remembers the room.

considerations.title: Two briefs, one building
considerations.text: Lobby work can be singular and architectural. Guest floors need a series that varies without competing.

considerations.title: Corridors are long and dim
considerations.text: Repeating series at consistent intervals give a corridor rhythm; single large pieces get lost in it.

considerations.title: Fixings matter
considerations.text: Guest-room art is installed to resist being knocked straight. We fix accordingly rather than hanging on a hook.

name: Schools
pitch: Durable, inspiring murals for halls and libraries.
headline: Walls that teach something on the way past
intro: School corridors are walked thousands of times a term by people who will remember them for decades. That is a rare opportunity and a demanding brief: the work has to survive contact, mean something to a fifteen-year-old, and not embarrass the school in five years.

considerations.title: It will be touched
considerations.text: At pupil height, PVC foam or aluminium rather than MDF. This is not a preference, it is the difference between five years and one term.

considerations.title: Fire rating is asked first
considerations.text: PVC foam is self-extinguishing and thin gauges reach Class A under ASTM E84, which is why it is our default here. We send the supplier's test data with the quote rather than after it.

considerations.title: Words earn their place
considerations.text: Typography and calligraphy work well here — pupils actually read corridor walls, repeatedly.

name: Universities
pitch: Campus identity walls and department art programs.
headline: Art that gives a department its own character
intro: A campus is many buildings pretending to be one institution. Art is one of the few things that can hold that together while still letting a department feel distinct — a shared visual language, applied differently in engineering than in the library.

considerations.title: Programme it, do not decorate it
considerations.text: Planning art across a floor plan produces coherence that piece-by-piece buying never does.

considerations.title: Departments want their own voice
considerations.text: A shared palette with different subjects per department gives identity without fragmentation.

considerations.title: Phased budgets are normal
considerations.text: We plan the whole programme, then install in phases as budget releases.
